presentation.label: IMPROVED FLTR
presentation.summary: A base-width type on the FILTER page: the Rytm's analog filter as a high-pass and a low-pass in one, FRQ setting the base and a WID knob the width above it.
presentation.overview: Improved FLTR adds BW to the FILTER page's types, after PK. In BW the voice's own analog 2-pole filter runs as a band: FRQ sets the high-pass edge (the base), and RES's knob, which reads WID in this type, sets how far above it the low-pass edge sits, from one semitone to five octaves, with 6 dB/oct slopes. It stays analog: the filter's resonance is taken below stock's RES 0, which widens its band-pass (measured on a unit). FRQ, an LFO on it and the filter envelope move the whole band; an LFO or lock on WID changes its width. WID shows where the band's top edge is, in hertz, and the FILTER graph draws the band as the filter plays it.
highlights: BW after PK in the TYPE list: an analog high-pass and low-pass in one.
FRQ is the base; WID sets the width above it, 1 semitone to 5 octaves, shown as the top edge in hertz.
FRQ, LFO and the filter envelope move the whole band; LFO or locks on WID change its width.
The FILTER graph draws the band as measured on a unit.
All analog: no digital processing of the voice.
usage: Use a build containing Improved FLTR. On BD, press FILTER and turn TYP past PK: it reads BW, the knob shows a band, RES's knob now reads WID and the graph draws the band.
Turn FRQ to about 220 Hz and WID up: the band opens upward from 220 Hz; WID shows its top edge in hertz.
Turn FRQ: the whole band moves and keeps its width.
Add filter envelope with ENV: the band sweeps on each hit.
Lock FRQ or WID on trigs, or point an LFO at either, as on any type.

access.location: FILTER page: TYP (BW), FRQ and RES's knob (WID).
steps: Turn TYP past PK to BW.
Turn FRQ for the base and WID for the width.

controls.name: FILTER > TYP
controls.doc: Past PK: BW, the base-width band. Every other type is stock's.

controls.name: FILTER > FRQ
controls.doc: In BW: the high-pass edge (the base), on stock's scale (a semitone a step, 440 Hz at 60).

controls.name: FILTER > WID (RES's knob)
controls.doc: In BW: the width, 0 to 127 for 0 to 59.5 semitones above FRQ (held to 1 semitone at least); it shows the band's top edge in hertz. Its label and name read WID and Width while the selected sound is BW.

controls.name: FILTER > ENV
controls.doc: In BW: moves the analog cutoff, the band's centre, so both edges move together and the width stays.

limitations: Built for OS 1.74 only, on Modwerk's Rytm base.
A kit with BW plays it as PK on a build without the module (stock's own clamp) and shows a blank TYP picture; nothing else changes.
Widths from 1 semitone to 5 octaves, 6 dB/oct slopes; a wider band is quieter (about 7 dB down at 4.5 octaves) and there is no make-up gain.
On a unit the band's top edge landed within about 3 % of WID, its bottom edge 2 to 18 % above FRQ (most for the widest band); the analog filter moves a few percent from run to run.
The filter envelope moves the whole band; it cannot move the base or the width alone.
RES keeps its value when TYP changes: a BW width read as stock resonance can self-oscillate loudly; set RES after leaving BW.
While the selected sound is BW, lists that name parameters (performance, scene) call every RES Width.

claims: audio:filter cutoff, resonance and type stores
param:FILTER RES names (WID / Width on BW)
ui:value text of FILTER TYP and RES
ui:FILTER page graph for type 7 (drawn by the module)

load.display: About 35 instructions a BW voice an audio block, 5 for any other type; graph and texts in the UI only
load.conditions: Counted in src/band.s: the filter routine's stores are taken by one jump; a stock type adds a compare and two jumps, BW adds the width, centre and table interpolation. Not measured on a unit.

hardware.summary: 0.1.0's BW ran on npp1993's (the author's) Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74, from RAM in the author's private combined test images with a development base and a USB test link, run by the author's automated rig with the author's go, 23 November 2026. IFD2 (the combined set FXCD): the analog words BW sends (cutoff, resonance, BP switch code) as computed, TYP's knob stopping at BW. IFC5 (the combined set FXC8): the same and the band's edges measured with noise through the filter, top edges within about 3 % of WID, bottom edges 2 to 18 % above FRQ.
limitations: Run by an automated rig; the author listened only informally.
The edges were measured on the FXC8 set; on the newer FXCD set the measuring machine's noise did not sound on the unit, so only the analog words and TYP were checked there.
The FILTER graph and texts were checked in the emulator, not photographed on the unit.
Not run: the package flashed, a project save and load, a power cycle, the audio load.

tests.summary: On the author's MKII from RAM (IFD2, IFC5; 23 Nov 2026): BW's analog words, TYP's knob, and the band's edges measured (IFC5). rytm-emu: the graph and labels against recorded references, TYP's knob, the analog words; sdk/tests/test_improved_fltr_table.py keeps the width table in step with the calibration.
